title: Kenya Launches National AI and Robotics Youth Initiative in ITU Five-Country Africa Programme
detail: The Communications Authority of Kenya, in partnership with the ITU, the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy, and the Ministry of Education, announced a national initiative on May 12, 2026 to push AI and robotics education for young Kenyans aged 10–18. The programme includes innovation hubs, robotics competitions, teacher training workshops (Training of Trainers), distribution of robotics kits to schools, and national innovation showcases. Kenya is part of the ITU's five-country Africa AI and Robotics Youth Training Programme rollout spanning Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Nigeria, and South Africa — a coordinated effort to embed AI competency in secondary education systems across the continent's largest digital economies. The initiative directly targets the skills dimension of Africa's 63% mobile internet usage gap by building technology confidence among youth with network coverage but low digital competency.

title: Starlink and Amazon Leo Positioned for Combined ~$1B BEAD Satellite Allocation Under Policy Shift
detail: Reporting published on May 12, 2026 revealed that under the current US administration, SpaceX's Starlink and Amazon Leo (formerly Project Kuiper) are positioned to receive a combined approximately $1 billion from the $42.45 billion BEAD broadband program — earmarked to connect more than a fifth of currently unserved US communities via LEO satellite internet. This represents a significant policy shift away from the Biden-era preference for fiber-only BEAD deployments toward technology-neutral satellite allocation. The satellite-first approach for some BEAD segments is justified by faster deployment timelines versus multi-year fiber construction projects, though critics note satellite service has higher long-term costs and lower shared capacity than fiber infrastructure. Amazon Leo is simultaneously conducting enterprise beta with partners including Verizon, AT&T, Vodafone, and Vodacom as it targets mid-2026 commercial launch.
